messages.text: Hey all, should we lock in our November hiking trip? Let's use this thread to decide where we're going.
Yes! I've been thinking Patagonia. Torres del Paine has been on my list for years.
I'd like the Dolomites. Hut-to-hut hiking would be amazing.
I'll throw in Banff. It's close and the flights are cheap.
What about Yosemite? Even cheaper and no passports needed.
Any of those work for me. I just need to be back by Sunday the 22nd.
Good to know, Leo. So the dates would be Nov 14 to 21?
Nov 14-21 works for me.
Works for me too.
Same here, I already put it on my calendar.
I'm free those dates too.
Nov 14-21 is perfect, that gets me home on the 21st.
Great, dates are locked: Nov 14 to 21, seven days.
Next, budget. I was thinking around $2,500 per person all in. Does that work?
$2,500 is fine for me.
Fine for me. Banff would come in well under that.
Works for me, though I'd rather come in lower if we can.
$2,500 works. Patagonia flights would eat a lot of it though.
$2,500 is OK by me.
What matters most to everyone? I care mostly about great hiking and good views.
Same, hiking quality first. Then cost.
Hiking first, and I'd like some variety in the trail types.
For me it's cost and weather. I don't love cold rain.
Weather too. And how easy the logistics are.
Hiking and views, like Sam. I'm flexible on everything else.
Patagonia flights are usually around $1,300 round trip for us, I checked last week.
The Dolomites are around $900 for flights, but hut availability in November could be tight.
Banff in mid-November is usually snowy, so I'd guess a lot of trails would be hard to hike.
Yosemite is easy to reach, but I think it's a bit tame for a week of hiking.
Patagonia in November is spring, so it should be mild with longer days.
Thanks all. So flights are about $1,300 for Patagonia and $900 for the Dolomites.
Given the snow thing, I'm happy to drop Banff. Let's not hike in a foot of snow.
I'll drop Yosemite too, it's better for a long weekend anyway.
So it's down to Patagonia and the Dolomites?
Yes. And honestly the hut availability worries me for the Dolomites in November.
Then Patagonia sounds better to me on the weather too.
Anyone still strongly for the Dolomites?
Not strongly. I'm happy with Patagonia, it's been on my list too.
Patagonia works for me. Flights are a stretch but still inside $2,500.
I'm in for Patagonia too.
Great, I'm obviously in for Patagonia.
Patagonia, yes.
Then Patagonia it is. Are all six of us agreed?
Yes, all in. Torres del Paine, here we come.
Yes from me.
Yes.
Yes, I'm in.
Yes, count me in.
I'm in too.
Morning! I'll book flights by Friday. Please all confirm your passports are valid.
Passport is good. I'll look at W trek itineraries and post options tonight.
Passport is fine. I'll research refugio and campsite bookings.
Passport good. I'll look at travel insurance and post options here.
Passport good. I'll set up a shared expense sheet.
Passport good. I'll check gear rental in Puerto Natales.
Also, I'll find out the best way to get from Punta Arenas to the park.
Great. I'll ping the group when I hear back from the refugios.
Nice, this went fast. Thanks Sam for organizing.
Agreed, thanks Sam. Sheet link coming tomorrow.
Thanks all, this is going to be a great trip.
